questions.instructions: Code this PAGE for the named institution only, using only what the page says. Does it document a generative-AI activity at this institution? If several values fit, take the first in this order.

criteria.text:
The page documents a specific generative-AI activity AT THIS institution: its own GenAI tool, pilot, policy or guidance on GenAI, procurement, deployment, or institution-directed staff GenAI training. The text must be explicitly generative AI (LLMs, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, AI chatbots, AI-generated content or equivalents) and tied to this institution, not only to a national programme or another body. The activity must be carried out or adopted by the named institution itself. Exclude activity by a parent, higher-level or neighbouring body (e.g. a district, county, regency, region, consortium or city department when the named institution is a village, ward or sub-unit), by a similarly named organisation or company, and pages by vendors that only use the place name. Generic 'AI', 'artificial intelligence', 'smart' systems, automation, analytics, prediction, transcription, translation, image or video recognition, or traditional machine-learning tools do not count unless the page says the tool generates text, images, audio, code or other content, or names a generative product or model (e.g. ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Claude, an LLM, an AI chatbot or AI assistant).

Rules:
1. The vocabulary has 9 values: the 8 below plus `not_assessable`, set mechanically when a page was not reviewed, never a classifier answer, not blocking institution `no`, and left out of the base for institution-level rates; in published summaries it is reported as `unknown` and stays a coding value; `page_review_state` keeps only pipeline failures; v2.5 rows stay unconverted and are mapped by the translation table.
2. Generative-AI wording: the re-pilot 2 wording governs (SRC-7 L34-45), including that a named "AI chatbot or AI assistant" counts as a generative product; `system_prompt.md` L15 rule ("chatbot" alone is not evidence) is amended to match. A named "AI chatbot" or "AI assistant" counts as generative and overrides the rule-based-chatbot exclusion (contract L12) for that naming.
3. S1 a: translation counts as generative AI only when the page ties it to a named generative product or says a language model produces it.
4. WS10 D1 action boundary: a public-facing GenAI event or educational programme is not a qualifying activity; an event page can support a separate record only when it documents the institution's own adoption, procurement, deployment or governance.
5. An activity carried out by an organisational unit of the named institution (department, office, service) counts for the named institution. An activity of its parent, a sibling, or a separate court, board or authority does not, unless the page says the named institution takes part.
6. A joint activity counts when the page names this institution as a participant.

questions.instructions: What kind of document is this page?

criteria.text:
The page is, or is one entry in, a structured list of AI or algorithmic systems kept by a government body, with several entries in a common format (inventory, register, catalogue, algorithmic transparency record in a standard template), **and the list covers more than one institution** (a national or sectoral register, a standard-template record series across agencies).

Rules:
1. Any government-kept multi-entry list in a common format counts as a register, including one institution's own list; single-institution and cross-institution registers are separate values (CX-10, CX-10b). `disclosure_scope` (§3) still codes whole-of-government vs multi-institution for cross-institution registers; `register_single_institution` must carry `disclosure_scope` = `single_institution` (QC check).
2. The obligation must be named on the page, except that it may be inferred from the document's genre **when the document's title names AI or algorithmic reporting**. Otherwise a statutory annual report or a compliance report under a rule not about AI is `formal_record`. This is the one stated exception to CX-03.
3. (1) A city's entry in a national algorithm register describing its chatbot → `register_cross_institution`. (2) A ministry annual-report section headed with the regulation that requires AI-use reporting → `mandated_report`. (3) Council minutes approving a Copilot licence → `formal_record`. (4) A mayor's press release launching a chatbot → `informal_official`. (5) A trade-press article about that chatbot → `third_party`. (6) A city web page that lists its five AI tools in a table it made itself → `register_single_institution`.
4. Re-word CX-12/13: `mandated_report` only when the obligation concerns reporting on AI, algorithms or digital systems, named on the page; genre inference allowed only for documents whose title names AI/algorithmic reporting. Otherwise statutory annual reports code `formal_record`.
5. CX-12/13: a document produced to meet a reporting obligation that concerns reporting on AI, algorithms or digital systems (statutory annual-report section, compliance or transparency report under a rule). The obligation must be named on the page, except that it may be inferred from the document's genre when the document's title names AI or algorithmic reporting. Otherwise a statutory annual report or a compliance report under a rule not about AI is formal_record.
6. Add those reports to the same sentence.
7. The page's kind cannot be determined from its text (e.g. an archived fragment with no header).

criteria.text:
The page states that this activity was tested, evaluated, audited or monitored **and** reports a result (a metric, a finding or a conclusion).

Rules:
1. A requirement to carry out a risk or impact assessment is **not** `required_or_planned`; it belongs to `has_risk_assessment` alone (consistent with CX-37).
2. A clause requiring periodic review of the GenAI policy itself is `not_documented`, unless it requires testing, monitoring or evaluation of GenAI tools or their outputs; then it counts as `required_or_planned`. This includes any policy with a GenAI section (e.g. a general IT policy).
3. A required pre-use review that mixes fitness-for-purpose with security or compliance checks counts as `required_or_planned`. A pure risk or impact assessment requirement stays under CX-32b.
4. No negative value. A page saying no evaluation was done or planned is `not_documented`.
5. A performance figure counts as `results_reported` only if the page also describes the activity behind it (a test, a pilot review, a survey, an audit, monitoring); otherwise `not_documented`.
6. A risk or impact assessment counts here only if it reports testing or measured performance; otherwise it belongs to `has_risk_assessment` alone.
7. A vendor's performance claim counts only if the page names the institution or an independent body as the evaluator.
8. A pilot stage alone is `not_documented`. "The pilot will be evaluated" is `required_or_planned`; "the pilot evaluation found …" is `results_reported`.
